2607.22692.title: Risk Governance for Generative AI Mental Health Support: A Multi-Turn Safety Architecture
2607.22692.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for emotional support despite lacking mechanisms to safely govern evolving mental health risk. Existing safety approaches primarily detect risk but rarely shape how models respond as conversational risk unfolds. We developed a model-agnostic safety governance architecture that combines contextual risk detection, reasoning-based verification, and protocol-guided response generation for multi-turn mental health interactions. Synthetic conversations grounded in real-world mental health narratives were used to evaluate the architecture's performance, tested with GPT-5-chat and Qwen3.5-27B, achieving high risk detection performance (specificity: 0.85 (95\%CI: 0.78;0.91), sensitivity: 0.92 (95\%CI: 0.88;0.95)) and increasing clinician-preferred escalation responses by 25.6--59.2pp while preserving rapport and connection. Performance remained stable across conversation length and generalized across both proprietary and open-source models. These findings demonstrate that clinically-grounded safety governance can extend beyond risk detection to improve how LLMs manage evolving mental health risk, providing a scalable framework for safer deployment across models.
2607.22692.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）越來越多地被用於情感支持，儘管缺乏安全管理不斷演變的心理健康風險的機制。現有的安全方法主要檢測風險，但很少影響模型在對話風險展開時的反應。我們開發了一種與模型無關的安全治理架構，結合了情境風險檢測、基於推理的驗證和協議引導的回應生成，用於多輪心理健康互動。基於現實世界心理健康敘事的合成對話被用來評估該架構的性能，並在GPT-5-chat和Qwen3.5-27B上進行測試，實現了高風險檢測性能（特異性：0.85（95\%CI：0.78；0.91），靈敏度：0.92（95\%CI：0.88；0.95）），並將臨床醫生首選的升級回應提高了25.6--59.2個百分點，同時保持了融洽和連結。性能在對話長度上保持穩定，並在專有模型和開源模型之間泛化。這些發現表明，臨床基礎的安全治理可以超越風險檢測，改善LLMs管理不斷演變的心理健康風險的方式，為更安全的模型部署提供可擴展的框架。
